sections.Objective:
Deliver `T013` so the read-code command help or local command documentation explains the new scoped-versus-broad trust behavior clearly.

This task documents the routing policy once the implementation is settled.
sections.Relevant Domains:
- `Human-First Decisions`: maintainers need documentation for when markdown and broad trust work are expected.
- `Spec and Process-First`: the command or plan docs must reflect the approved implementation contract.
- `Code Reading and Discovery`: this is documentation for a heavily used internal reading command.
sections.Candidate Design Slices:
- `Slice PL-02 - Broad Discovery and Conditional Escalation` — explain when broad queries still use markdown-aware discovery and when escalation occurs.
- `Slice PL-03 - Benchmark and Regression Coverage` — keep the docs aligned with the accepted benchmark corpus. Primary seams: `scripts/read_code.py` help text or module docstring and `specs/031-speed-up-vector-context/plan.md`.
sections.Proposed Solution:
- Update the nearest `read_code.py` help text, parser guidance, or module-level command documentation so it explains scoped versus broad routing and when trust or fallback escalation occurs.
- Update `plan.md` or related feature docs only as needed so the approved artifact set matches the final command behavior.
- Keep the documentation concise and operational: exact symbol/path reads follow the scoped contract; broad discovery keeps mixed behavior and conditional escalation.
- Change the following artifacts in this task: the relevant help/doc seam in `scripts/read_code.py` and `specs/031-speed-up-vector-context/plan.md`.
sections.Current Repo Behavior:
- `_parse_context_args(...)` documents the command syntax and accepted flags, including `--path`, `--candidate-index`, and `--content-type`.
- The repo docs and plan currently describe the feature work, but the settled command-level broad-versus-scoped trust behavior is not yet codified as user-facing or maintainer-facing help text.
- The parser currently accepts the command options but does not by itself explain the new trust policy.
sections.Target Behavior:
- Maintainers can tell when `read_code context` behaves as a scoped read versus a broad read.
- The docs explain when markdown remains part of discovery and when escalation happens.
- The feature plan and local command help stay aligned with the implemented routing contract.
sections.Reuse Candidates:
- Reuse the parser/help seams around `_parse_context_args(...)`.
- Reuse the approved wording and behavior split already captured in `plan.md` and `tasks.md`.
- Reuse the existing command vocabulary rather than inventing new conceptual terms.
sections.Required Edits:
- Add or update concise help text in `scripts/read_code.py` that explains scoped versus broad trust routing.
- Update `specs/031-speed-up-vector-context/plan.md` only where the approved artifact should reflect the final policy.
- Keep the documentation focused on actual behavior, not implementation internals.

sections.Tests To Add Or Update:
- No new automated test module is required unless the repo already snapshots help text.
- Validation command: rerun the targeted unit and integration commands from the settled implementation tasks, then verify the updated docs by reading the affected sections.
- If a help-text assertion exists nearby, update it instead of adding a second documentation-only harness.
sections.Acceptance Criteria:
- The local command help or doc seam explains scoped-versus-broad trust behavior.
- The docs state that markdown remains relevant for broad behavior questions.
- The feature docs and command docs do not contradict each other.
sections.Done Criteria:

- Any corresponding plan wording is aligned.

sections.Constraints And Invariants:

- Keep documentation concise and behavior-focused.
- Do not let the docs drift from the approved feature artifacts or implemented behavior.
